## `` com.cra.figaro.algorithm.structured.strategy.refine.BacktrackingStrategy.refine ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/algorithm/structured/strategy/refine/BacktrackingStrategy.html#refine-fffff482)

```scala
def refine(comp: ProblemComponent[_], depth: Int): Unit
```

Decompose a single problem component by recursively decomposing components on which it depends, then generating the range for each component. This guarantees that when ranges are created, all components on which a component depends (at that depth) will have been processed.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` comp: ProblemComponent[_] ``; `` depth: Int ``.

Returns: `` Unit ``.

Source contract/attributes: Decompose a single problem component by recursively decomposing components on which it depends, then generating the range for each component. This guarantees that when ranges are created, all components on which a component depends (at that depth) will have been processed. As a rule, this method never works in the other direction. If component B depends (directly or indirectly) on component A, then calling decompose on A will never recursively call decompose on component B. This is to avoid infinite loops, and to guarantee that the range of A does not unpredictably change in the middle of a call to decompose A. Once the range has been created, the depths map is updated. If any previously visited components depend on comp, this method updates those components in a top-down manner. Value parameters comp Component to decompose. This strategy never decomposes a component more than once, so if the component is fully refined or has already been expanded to the desired depth, this method does nothing. depth Depth of expansion with respect to this component. Attributes

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.refine(comp, depth)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.algorithm.structured.strategy.refine.DepthFirstStrategy.refine ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/algorithm/structured/strategy/refine/DepthFirstStrategy.html#refine-fffff39d)

```scala
def refine(comp: ProblemComponent[_]): Unit
```

Refine a single problem component by recursively refining components on which it depends, then generating the range for each component. This guarantees that when ranges are created, all components on which a component depends will have been processed.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` comp: ProblemComponent[_] ``.

Returns: `` Unit ``.

Source contract/attributes: Refine a single problem component by recursively refining components on which it depends, then generating the range for each component. This guarantees that when ranges are created, all components on which a component depends will have been processed. As a rule, this method never works in the other direction. If component B depends (directly or indirectly) on component A, then calling decompose on A will never recursively call decompose on component B. This is to avoid infinite loops, and to guarantee that the range of A does not unpredictably change in the middle of a call to decompose A. Once the range has been created, the component will be added to the set done, and (if applicable) the component is marked as fully enumerated or refined. Value parameters comp Component to refine. This strategy never refines a component more than once, so if the component is fully refined or in the set done, this method does nothing. Attributes

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.refine(comp)
```

## `` com.cra.figaro.algorithm.structured.strategy.refine.RecursionDepthStrategy.refine ``

[Full Scaladoc entry](../../target/out/jvm/scala-3.9.0/figaro/api/com/cra/figaro/algorithm/structured/strategy/refine/RecursionDepthStrategy.html#refine-fffff39d)

```scala
def refine(comp: ProblemComponent[_]): Unit
```

Refine a single problem component by recursively refining components on which it depends, then generating the range for each component. This guarantees that when ranges are created, all components on which a component depends will have been processed.

Type parameters: none.

Parameters, list 1: `` comp: ProblemComponent[_] ``.

Returns: `` Unit ``.

Source contract/attributes: Refine a single problem component by recursively refining components on which it depends, then generating the range for each component. This guarantees that when ranges are created, all components on which a component depends will have been processed. As a rule, this method never works in the other direction. If component B depends (directly or indirectly) on component A, then calling decompose on A will never recursively call decompose on component B. This is to avoid infinite loops, and to guarantee that the range of A does not unpredictably change in the middle of a call to decompose A. Once the range has been created, the component will be added to the set done, and (if applicable) the component is marked as fully enumerated or refined. Value parameters comp Component to refine. This strategy never refines a component more than once, so if the component is fully refined or in the set done, this method does nothing. Attributes Inherited from: DepthFirstStrategy

Invocation template:

```scala
receiver.refine(comp)
```
